Subject: Post-demo: Hyperscaler Gap Matrix & SLO probing plan

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next-steps plan so we can move from evaluation -> pilot without re-work.

Highlights from the demo:
- Redwood inference runtime shows consistent 95/99 latency tail improvements vs the public hyperscaler endpoint in our baseline tests (summary attached).
- Your primary concerns: regional failover behavior, tenant-level rate-limits, and plausible error-budget burn under sustained burst traffic.

What we’re proposing (attached files):
1) Gap matrix (hyperscaler_gap_matrix_v1.xlsx) — row-by-row comparison versus the major hyperscalers: failover windows, default RPS limits, burst behavior, KV cache semantics, and cold-start characteristics.
2) SLO probing plan (probe-script.sh + redwood-performance-runbook.pdf) — a short, non-invasive probe plan to exercise 99/99.9 tail behavior, simultaneous multi-region routing, and controlled error-budget burn profiles.

Immediate asks from BrightPay to schedule tests:
- Can you provide a staging endpoint and an SRE contact for credentials? (we’ll only run on staging during agreed windows)
- Any constraints on maximum simulated QPS for staging?

Proposed timeline:
- Thu 6/11: confirm staging creds and test windows
- Fri 6/12: baseline synthetic probe (non-invasive, 1 hour)
- Mon 6/15: full probe (multi-region, 3-4 hours) + shared Datadog dashboards

If that works I’ll loop in our Solutions Engineer (Ben) and Technical SRE (Rishi) to run the probes and share a gap matrix with concrete remediation recommendations.

Attachments: hyperscaler_gap_matrix_v1.xlsx (summary), probe-script.sh (small harness), redwood-performance-runbook.pdf (methodology)

Best,

Appreciate the recap and the artifacts. A couple quick clarifying questions before we confirm the windows: 

1) Rate limits: can you call out Redwood’s per-tenant default RPS and burst window? Our staging environment caps at 2k RPS but we want to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
2) Failover behavior: when you say "multi-region routing," what is the observed time-to-first-success when a primary region fails (we care about <30s as a target)?
3) Error budget policy: we want to understand how you define and surface error-budget burn (alerts, dashboards, automated fallbacks).

I’ll coordinate with Angela (our infra lead) for a staging endpoint and give you a contact by EOD. We are aiming for the 6/12 baseline if it’s light.

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hyperscaler Gap Matrix & SLO probing plan

Alex / team —

Quick answers to the three bullets and proposed test knobs:

1) Rate limits: default tenant-level steady-state is 500 RPS, with a controlled burst window up to 2,000 RPS for short windows (30–120s) depending on tenant tier. For Dedicated customers we can raise steady-state limits as part of the pilot contract. We’ll honor any per-test QPS caps you require for staging.

2) Failover timing: in our multi-region tests we typically see model-level failover to the warm-standby (same model family) in 8–18s depending on KV cache priming. The matrix attached highlights delta vs hyperscalers where region failover often triggers cold-starts and longer DNS propagation times; our routing uses pinned route failover + model variant substitution to keep TTFB low.

3) Error-budget & observability: we define SLOs at token-level latency (p95/p99/p99.9) and availability (successful-response-rate). Our runbook will raise alerts at 5% burn over a rolling 7d window and trigger automated fallback policies (route to regional replica or lower-cost model variant) at 10% burn. We will share Datadog dashboards during the test window and create a temporary alert channel for your SREs.

Planned probe knobs (what we’ll run on staging if you approve):
- Controlled ramp to target QPS (steady-state 500 -> 2,000 RPS in 15m)
- Tail-latency probes (95/99/99.9) with synthetic payloads matching your average prompt length
- Error-injection at 1% cadence to measure graceful degradation and automated fallback accuracy
- Multi-region failover simulation via route cutover (observe cache warm-up and TTFB delta)

Operational asks for staging access:
- An endpoint + API key with explicit timeframe + max QPS cap (if any)
- Contact for an SRE to coordinate scheduling and network allowlists

If you want, I can also prepare a short one-page commit for a 30-day pilot (pricing + support terms) and send it for signature — we have a DocuSign link ready.

Attachments: probe-script.sh, redwood-performance-runbook.pdf

Thanks,

Ben Carter

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Looking forward to the probe results.

—Alex
